sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's digital economy is structurally driven by rising internet penetration and a young, mobile-first population, supporting long-term growth for local tech platforms.
US-listed IT services firms like ACN and CTSH benefit from durable enterprise digital transformation spending, which is resilient to rate cycles.
Cloud and cybersecurity demand, reflected in ZBRA and GDDY, remains a secular driver as businesses globally prioritize data security and operational efficiency.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's tech sector underperformed today, but selective movers like MLPT and 1810 show local resilience. Watch for a bottom in US-listed names like ACN and WDAY, which signal stabilizing demand. Focus on Indonesian digital infrastructure plays and IT services firms with US exposure for near-term re-entry.

themes: Insurance penetration in Indonesia remains below 3% of GDP, creating a multi-decade compounding opportunity for underwriters like BRO and ERIE as middle-class risk awareness rises.
Digital transaction volumes are accelerating 25%+ YoY, structurally boosting fee-based revenue for payment processors and brokers (MTWI, YULE) independent of loan growth cycles.
Regulatory push for mandatory TPL auto insurance by 2025 will force a step-change in premium pools, directly benefiting domestic composite insurers (MGNA, MRSH) with existing distribution networks.
sectors.ai: Indonesia financials lagged US peers today, but the sharp rally in MGNA (+34%) signals selective value discovery in underfollowed names. Favor brokers/insurers (MTWI, BRO) for structural fee-income growth as BI holds rates; avoid general banks until NIM trough is confirmed in Q3.

themes: Nickel downstreaming is a multi-year structural driver, with Indonesia's ban on raw ore exports forcing global investment into local smelters and HPAL plants, benefiting companies like ALKA.
Coal demand from China and India remains resilient despite ESG pressures, as Indonesia's low-cost, high-calorific coal producers maintain pricing power and export volume growth.
Government's push for energy transition via geothermal and solar creates a long-term opportunity for domestic EPC contractors and renewable asset owners, though near-term earnings rely on coal.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's mining & energy sector underperformed US peers today, but ALKA's +24.73% surge signals strong local nickel play momentum. Capitalize on this by overweighting downstream nickel processors and coal exporters, as structural demand from EV battery supply chains and China's energy needs remain durable drivers.

sectors.name: Entertainment, Media & Consumer Services

Local content creators and gaming platforms (e.g., PGLI) benefit from rising smartphone penetration and a young demographic that prioritizes in-app purchases over linear entertainment.
Regulatory tailwinds from Indonesia's Omnibus Law and eased foreign ownership rules are attracting global media partnerships, boosting M&A and capital inflows into domestic consumer services.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's entertainment sector underperformed US peers (-1.69% vs +2.42%), but DOOH and PGLI surged on local ad-spend rotation. Favor DOOH for structural out-of-home recovery and PGLI for gaming monetization tailwinds. Avoid broad ID exposure; focus on digital-native sub-segments with pricing power and rising middle-class consumption.

sectors.ai: Rotate into infrastructure plays (UNI, JUP, ADA) and RWA tokens (ONDO) as the market consolidates; BEAT's 28.8% surge is a low-liquidity outlier—avoid chasing. Position for a Q2 regulatory catalyst in Indonesia's crypto licensing framework, which could re-rate compliant tokens.
